asks: Does a subscription sign-in change how Silo reads traffic?
answer: No. A subscription and an API key are read the same way: the credential a request carries changes nothing in how Silo reads it. The boundary decides whether to read a connection when it opens, from the host the program names, before any credential is sent. A kind of sign-in can change the host, the transport and the format, though: Codex under a ChatGPT sign-in talks to chatgpt.com, and with an API key to api.openai.com. So the hosts Silo reads, with their transport and format, are listed per provider and per kind of sign-in, and each is read only once the live checks of `reading-each-agent-program` cover it. Those checks, run for each version a recipe pins, are where a new host is found and added to the list. Model traffic to a host that is not on the list, such as a host a new version of a program starts to use, is not read, and Silo treats it as `program-that-cannot-be-read` says. Whether a kind of sign-in is read at all is not decided here. Where a provider's terms rule out reading one kind, that kind passes unread, as `program-that-cannot-be-read` says. When that kind shares a host with a kind Silo reads, as a Claude subscription and an Anthropic API key share api.anthropic.com, the two cannot be told apart before the connection is read, so the choice is made per computer and not per request, as `anthropic-reads-intermediate` does.
